_**Law of the Plainsman**_ is a Western television series starring Michael Ansara that aired on NBC from October 1, 1959, until September 22, 1960.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-slts-1)
The character of Native American Deputy U.S. Marshal Sam Buckhart was introduced in two episodes ("The Indian" and "The Raid") of the popular ABC Western television series _The Rifleman_ starring Chuck Connors. As with _The Rifleman_, this series was produced by Four Star Productions in association with Levy-Gardner-Laven Productions.
_Law of the Plainsman_ is distinctive in that it was one of the few television programs that featured a Native American as the lead character, a bold move for American network television at that time. Ansara had earlier appeared in the series _Broken Arrow_, having portrayed the Apache chief, Cochise. Ansara, however, was not Native American but of Syrian descent.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-Peterson-2)

Ansara played Sam Buckhart, an Apache Indian who saved the life of a U.S. Cavalry officer after an Indian ambush. When the officer later died, he left Sam money that was used for an education at private schools and Harvard University. After school, he returned to New Mexico where he became a Deputy U.S. Marshal working for U.S. Marshal Andy Morrison. He lived in a boarding house run by Martha Commager. Other continuing characters include 8-year old Tess Logan, an orphan who had been rescued by Buckhart,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-brooks-3) and a second Deputy U.S. Marshal, Billy Lordan.

_**Law of the Plainsman**_ is a Western television series starring Michael Ansara that aired on NBC from October 1, 1959, until September 22, 1960.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-slts-1)
The character of Native American Deputy U.S. Marshal Sam Buckhart was introduced in two episodes ("The Indian" and "The Raid") of the popular ABC Western television series _The Rifleman_ starring Chuck Connors. As with _The Rifleman_, this series was produced by Four Star Productions in association with Levy-Gardner-Laven Productions.
_Law of the Plainsman_ is distinctive in that it was one of the few television programs that featured a Native American as the lead character, a bold move for American network television at that time. Ansara had earlier appeared in the series _Broken Arrow_, having portrayed the Apache chief, Cochise. Ansara, however, was not Native American but of Syrian descent.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-Peterson-2)
texts.1:
Ansara played Sam Buckhart, an Apache Indian who saved the life of a U.S. Cavalry officer after an Indian ambush. When the officer later died, he left Sam money that was used for an education at private schools and Harvard University. After school, he returned to New Mexico where he became a Deputy U.S. Marshal working for U.S. Marshal Andy Morrison. He lived in a boarding house run by Martha Commager. Other continuing characters include 8-year old Tess Logan, an orphan who had been rescued by Buckhart,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-brooks-3) and a second Deputy U.S. Marshal, Billy Lordan.

_**Law of the Plainsman**_ is a Western television series starring Michael Ansara that aired on NBC from October 1, 1959, until September 22, 1960.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-slts-1)
The character of Native American Deputy U.S. Marshal Sam Buckhart was introduced in two episodes ("The Indian" and "The Raid") of the popular ABC Western television series _The Rifleman_ starring Chuck Connors. As with _The Rifleman_, this series was produced by Four Star Productions in association with Levy-Gardner-Laven Productions.
_Law of the Plainsman_ is distinctive in that it was one of the few television programs that featured a Native American as the lead character, a bold move for American network television at that time. Ansara had earlier appeared in the series _Broken Arrow_, having portrayed the Apache chief, Cochise. Ansara, however, was not Native American but of Syrian descent.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-Peterson-2)

Ansara played Sam Buckhart, an Apache Indian who saved the life of a U.S. Cavalry officer after an Indian ambush. When the officer later died, he left Sam money that was used for an education at private schools and Harvard University. After school, he returned to New Mexico where he became a Deputy U.S. Marshal working for U.S. Marshal Andy Morrison. He lived in a boarding house run by Martha Commager. Other continuing characters include 8-year old Tess Logan, an orphan who had been rescued by Buckhart,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_the_Plainsman#cite_note-brooks-3) and a second Deputy U.S. Marshal, Billy Lordan.

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_, also known as _**Big Brother: Celebrity Edition**_, is a reality televisionspin-off series of the American adaptation of _Big Brother_ created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") The series began on February 7, 2018, on CBS in the United States and is simulcast in Canada on Global. The series is filmed at CBS Studio Center in sound stage eighteen located in Studio City, Los Angeles. Julie Chen Moonves reprises her role as host from _Big Brother_ with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan also returning as executive producers. The series is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.
The premise of the series remained largely unchanged from the main edition of _Big Brother_, in which a group of contestants, known as "HouseGuests," who live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother House, with no contact from the outside world. The contestants compete in competitions for safety and for power over the household before voting each other out in an attempt to be the last HouseGuest remaining and win a grand prize. The difference from the parent series is the inclusion of "Celebrity" HouseGuests (those with notoriety prior to participating in the series), the time frame (a month as opposed to 3 months) and a smaller grand prize ($250,000 as opposed to $750,000)
Each season is also transmitted in real-time which allows for greater viewer participation in the form of _America's Vote_ where the public can give their favorite HouseGuest various prizes ranging from luxury items to advantage to help them survive inside the House. Prior to the live season finale, the viewers are able to vote for their _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with the winner getting an auxiliary prize of $25,000.

The first overall season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ worldwide premiered in the United Kingdom in 2001 while an American version of the format has been speculated since 2002. The first season of the American adaptation was announced during a live double eviction episode of the nineteenth regular season on September 7, 2017, by Julie Chen Moonves. The first season was scheduled during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The series premiere was the number one program for CBS attracting 7.27 million viewers and the highest-rated season premiere since _Big Brother 13_. The program was often covered in the media due to the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her political revelations in the first season.
In September 2021, CBS renewed _Celebrity Big Brother_ for a third season, which premiered on February 2, 2022.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Air_date-1)
In October 2025, CBS cancelled _Celebrity Big Brother_ after three seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2)

The series is a game show in which a group of celebrity contestants, referred to as HouseGuests, live in a custom-built set, known as the Big Brother House, constantly under video surveillance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3) While in the House, the HouseGuests are completely isolated from the outside world, meaning no phone, television, Internet, magazines, newspaper, or contact with those not in the House.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) This rule could be broken, however, in the event of a medical injury, a family emergency, or death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) The format of the series is mainly seen as a social experiment, and requires HouseGuests to interact with others who may have differing ideals, beliefs, and prejudices.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3.2-6) Though locked in the House, the HouseGuests are free to quit the game, though will not be allowed entry back into the game.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-4-7) Should a HouseGuest break the rules of the game, they could be expelled from the House,

and unable to return.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-5-8) The HouseGuests compete for a grand prize of $250,000 and the runner-up is awarded $50,000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9) Prior to the live finale the viewers are able to award their favorite HouseGuest of the season the title _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with a cash prize of $25,000.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9)

Title: We Just Got A Major Update For Celebrity Big Brother & It’s Not The News We Wanted
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
Published Dec 11, 2024, 11:44 AM EST
Lorianne Palinkas has been a reality television writer for Screen Rant for four years. After teaching middle school English for twenty years, she knows a thing or two about high drama, complicated alliances, and even singing competitions. Growing up in New York City gave her a solid foundation in the arts and culture.
**_Celebrity Big Brother_** is one of the most popular versions of the series, but a new update shed light on whether it'll be returning anytime soon. _Celebrity Big Brother_ is basically the same as the original version of the game, except that it lasts for one month instead of three. There's also no jury house. **_Celebrity Big Brother_ season 1 premiered in February 2018**, with Marissa Jaret Winokur taking home the grand prize. Season 2 debuted in January 2019, with Tamar Braxton being crowned the champion, while season 3 aired in February 2022, with Miesha Tate being voted the winner.
The _Celebrity Big Brother_ producers want to bring the show back, but it won't happen in 2025.
According to _EW_, the _Celebrity Big Brother_ producers want to bring the show back, but it won't happen in 2025. When the spin-off premiered in 2018, it aired against the Winter Olympics. It came back the following year but didn't return until 2022 when it once again was offered as an alternative to the Winter Olympics. However, in a few months, it'll be three years since the show's last installment. When **_EW_ asked _Celebrity Big Brother_ executive producer Allison Grodner when the show was coming back**, she replied, _"We've been saying the same thing!"_
Allison explained,_"If you look at it, and again, we can't speak for CBS, the history of Celebrity Big Brother has it going against the Winter Olympics."_ However, this wasn't the case for the 2019 season. Allison said, _"That's true. We did try the back-to-back, and **we've heard rumblings that [airing opposite the Olympics] might be the way that Celebrity is utilized.**"_

Although CBS seems to want to air _Celebrity Big Brother_ during the Winter Olympics, **Allison and her fellow executive producer Rich Meehan would like to bring the series back sooner**. Allison said, _"We can't speak for CBS, but we agree with you. We think Celebrity is its own thing and is worthy of being on every other year or annually. It's been a lot of fun, so we're hoping to see it come back."_
Rich stated that he would "_love_" to see _Celebrity Big Brother_ return. Unfortunately, **there are "_usually much bigger things in play_," like the network's schedule**. "_There are a lot of factors that are much bigger than Big Brother that go into that_," he said, adding, _"But we love doing it. It's really fun, and it would be great to do again. But sometimes we have to wait and see how many scripted shows are happening and all that stuff. There's a lot of other things that go into it."_ The Winter Olympics won't air until February 2026.
> We can't speak for CBS, but we agree with you. We think Celebrity is its own thing and is worthy of being on every other year or annually. It's been a lot of fun, so we're hoping to see it come back.

## What A Yearly Celebrity Big Brother Season Would Mean For CBS
### Fans Love Shortened Spin-Off Seasons
*   

*   

*      
*   

*
With three episodes airing a week plus the live feeds, _Big Brother_ is perhaps the most time-consuming show on TV. After the season ends, fans miss it greatly, and _Celebrity Big Brother_ can fill that void. In addition, in December 2023, **_Big Brother Reindeer Games_, which brought back _Big Brother_ legends in a shortened season, was created as another fantastic way to keep fans of the show entertained** while they eagerly awaited the new summer season.
However, **there's something special about _Celebrity Big Brother_ because it challenges the celebrity competitors in ways that they never imagined**. _Big Brother_ is a game that requires tremendous physical, mental, emotional, and social strength, and it's inspiring to watch the celebrities who take the game seriously and make it far, realize their full potential. Of course, it's also great fun to watch the crazy antics that ensue in the house as well.

## Our Take On Celebrity Big Brother Airing Annually
### The Series Is Highly Entertaining
*   

*   

*      
*      
*
_Celebrity Big Brother_ is one of the most outrageous versions of the show, especially because it allows fans to see their favorite celebrities in a completely new environment. **It's also thrilling when the celebrities end up being superfans of the show**, such as when Chris Kirkpatrick and Shanna Moakler brought their incredible strategies to _Celebrity Big Brother_ season 3. It would be so much fun to have an annual season of **_Celebrity Big Brother_** to look forward to every year. Hopefully, it'll be back before 2026.

## Big Brother bosses are plotting a twist
* * *
Follow Heatworld on Google
The New Year started with bad news for Big Brother fans when it was revealed that Celebrity Big Brother won't be going ahead in 2026 after show bosses decided to rest the format until next year.
However, it appears there is some good news for viewers as the civilian series is reportedly set for an exciting shake-up.
According to reports, this year's Big Brother - the fourth series on ITV - is being extended to its longest ever run which means fans will get more house action than ever before.
This year's Big Brother is going to be longer
© Shutterstock for Big Brother
The ITV reboot of Big Brother ran for six weeks for the first two series, with last year's instalment being extended by an extra week. However, producers are reportedly planning to extend the upcoming series by another seven days, boosting it to eight weeks.
A TV insider said, 'Despite the hold on the celeb version, ITV has always insisted that the programme is what they call a "priority reality format". So it’s reassuring to see plans like this being on the table.
'Extending by a week is something fans have been calling for as past runs have shown the action really only heats up in the latter days.'
Big Brother is hosted by Will Best and AJ Odudu © Vianney Le Caer/Shutterstock for Big Brother
They told The Sun, 'The civilian one is far cheaper to produce than celebrity so the return on investment is worth the while.
'ITV really is committed to the format and has lots of ideas to keep the civilian version as exciting as possible, with the extension being one of the options being considered.'
Although Celebrity Big Brother won't be on our screens this year, it will reportedly return next year on ITV2 instead of its usual home on ITV1.
The cast of Celebrity Big Brother 2025
© ITV Pictures
The decision to rest the show is said to be due to the cost of running the series and booking big name celebrity housemates.
Last year, ITV boss Kevin Lygo admitted the channel was 'in a battle about the price' with creators Endemol and said that moving to ITV will allow 'more interesting and niche' celebrities to be signed up.

## Big Brother bosses are plotting a twist
Earlier this month, an ITV spokesperson said, 'We are committed to both Celebrity Big Brother and Big Brother beyond 2025, and scheduling for any new series will be confirmed in due course. The show remains a priority reality format for us.'

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_, also known as _**Big Brother: Celebrity Edition**_, is a reality televisionspin-off series of the American adaptation of _Big Brother_ created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") The series began on February 7, 2018, on CBS in the United States and is simulcast in Canada on Global. The series is filmed at CBS Studio Center in sound stage eighteen located in Studio City, Los Angeles. Julie Chen Moonves reprises her role as host from _Big Brother_ with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan also returning as executive producers. The series is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.
The premise of the series remained largely unchanged from the main edition of _Big Brother_, in which a group of contestants, known as "HouseGuests," who live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother House, with no contact from the outside world. The contestants compete in competitions for safety and for power over the household before voting each other out in an attempt to be the last HouseGuest remaining and win a grand prize. The difference from the parent series is the inclusion of "Celebrity" HouseGuests (those with notoriety prior to participating in the series), the time frame (a month as opposed to 3 months) and a smaller grand prize ($250,000 as opposed to $750,000)
Each season is also transmitted in real-time which allows for greater viewer participation in the form of _America's Vote_ where the public can give their favorite HouseGuest various prizes ranging from luxury items to advantage to help them survive inside the House. Prior to the live season finale, the viewers are able to vote for their _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with the winner getting an auxiliary prize of $25,000.

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_, also known as _**Big Brother: Celebrity Edition**_, is a reality televisionspin-off series of the American adaptation of _Big Brother_ created by [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") The series began on February 7, 2018, on CBS in the United States and is simulcast in Canada on Global. The series is filmed at CBS Studio Center in sound stage eighteen located in Studio City, Los Angeles. Julie Chen Moonves reprises her role as host from _Big Brother_ with Allison Grodner and Rich Meehan also returning as executive producers. The series is produced by Fly on the Wall Entertainment in association with Endemol Shine North America.
The premise of the series remained largely unchanged from the main edition of _Big Brother_, in which a group of contestants, known as "HouseGuests," who live in a purpose-built house, known as the Big Brother House, with no contact from the outside world. The contestants compete in competitions for safety and for power over the household before voting each other out in an attempt to be the last HouseGuest remaining and win a grand prize. The difference from the parent series is the inclusion of "Celebrity" HouseGuests (those with notoriety prior to participating in the series), the time frame (a month as opposed to 3 months) and a smaller grand prize ($250,000 as opposed to $750,000)
Each season is also transmitted in real-time which allows for greater viewer participation in the form of _America's Vote_ where the public can give their favorite HouseGuest various prizes ranging from luxury items to advantage to help them survive inside the House. Prior to the live season finale, the viewers are able to vote for their _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with the winner getting an auxiliary prize of $25,000.

The first overall season of _Celebrity Big Brother_ worldwide premiered in the United Kingdom in 2001 while an American version of the format has been speculated since 2002. The first season of the American adaptation was announced during a live double eviction episode of the nineteenth regular season on September 7, 2017, by Julie Chen Moonves. The first season was scheduled during the February 2018 sweeps period to counterprogramNBC's coverage of the 2018 Winter Olympics. The series premiere was the number one program for CBS attracting 7.27 million viewers and the highest-rated season premiere since _Big Brother 13_. The program was often covered in the media due to the inclusion of Omarosa Manigault and her political revelations in the first season.
In September 2021, CBS renewed _Celebrity Big Brother_ for a third season, which premiered on February 2, 2022.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Air_date-1)
In October 2025, CBS cancelled _Celebrity Big Brother_ after three seasons.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-2)

The series is a game show in which a group of celebrity contestants, referred to as HouseGuests, live in a custom-built set, known as the Big Brother House, constantly under video surveillance.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3) While in the House, the HouseGuests are completely isolated from the outside world, meaning no phone, television, Internet, magazines, newspaper, or contact with those not in the House.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) This rule could be broken, however, in the event of a medical injury, a family emergency, or death.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4) The format of the series is mainly seen as a social experiment, and requires HouseGuests to interact with others who may have differing ideals, beliefs, and prejudices.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-3.2-6) Though locked in the House, the HouseGuests are free to quit the game, though will not be allowed entry back into the game.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-4-7) Should a HouseGuest break the rules of the game, they could be expelled from the House,

and unable to return.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-2-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-5-8) The HouseGuests compete for a grand prize of $250,000 and the runner-up is awarded $50,000.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-1-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9) Prior to the live finale the viewers are able to award their favorite HouseGuest of the season the title _America's Favorite HouseGuest_ with a cash prize of $25,000.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(American_TV_series)#cite_note-Format-6-9)

_**Celebrity Big Brother**_ is a British television reality television based on the Dutch show _Big Brother_, created by producer [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") in 1997,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-BB1Article-1) which aired from 9 March 2001 to 10 September 2018, and again since 4 March 2024. The show follows a number of celebrity contestants, known as housemates, who were isolated from the outside world for an extended period of time in a custom-built house. Each week, one of the housemates is evicted by a public vote, with the last housemate named the winner. The series takes its name from the character in George Orwell's 1949 novel _Nineteen Eighty-Four_.

_Celebrity Big Brother_ began as a one-time spin-off series to the original _Big Brother UK_ and premiered on Channel 4 on 9 March 2001. Following the successful first series, the show returned the following year for a second series. Though the show did not air for the next two years, it returned in 2005 and 2006. Following the highly controversial fifth series in 2007, the show did not return in 2008. It did air in 2009, but it was officially axed after the seventh series in 2010 when Channel 4 chose to cancel the programme as well as the main series.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-3) Despite this, it was picked up by Channel 5, and _Celebrity Big Brother_ returned in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-4) Between 2012 and 2018, two editions of _Celebrity Big Brother_ aired each year, with one airing in January and one airing following the conclusion of the civilian series in August. The show was initially hosted by Davina McCall from its inception to its cancellation by Channel 4. Despite being offered the position of host following the show's move to Channel 5, McCall chose not to return. Brian Dowling, who had won on _Big Brother 2_ and _Ultimate Big Brother_, replaced McCall as the host of the series.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-5) Dowling hosted the eighth to eleventh series, before being replaced by Emma Willis from the twelfth series until the show's cancellation on Channel 5 following the twenty-second series.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-6) Following the show's relaunch on ITV in March 2024, AJ Odudu and Will Best will host the show from the twenty-third series onwards.

Marcus Bentley has narrated the series since its inception in 2001.
Much like its predecessor, _Celebrity Big Brother_ was met with commercial success and has also received extensive media coverage and publicity since it premiered. It has been covered in spin-off series such as _Big Brother's Big Mouth_ and _Big Brother's Bit on the Side_, which also covered the main series.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-8) Similar to the parent series, _Celebrity Big Brother_ has been the source of much controversy and criticism, most notably during the 2007 series. Following this, a spin-off series known as _Big Brother: Celebrity Hijack_ aired in 2008 in the place of _Celebrity Big Brother_. It has been noted that numerous celebrities who have appeared on the series have become more prominent figures in the media than before.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-12)
On 14 September 2018, Channel 5 announced that _Big Brother_ and _Celebrity Big Brother_ would not be returning to the channel after the end of the nineteenth regular series.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-13) The twenty-second series of _Celebrity Big Brother_ ended on 10 September 2018 and was the final series to air on Channel 5.

In August 2022, ITV plc announced that they were reviving _Big Brother_. The series relaunched in October 2023, which subsequently led to media speculation as to whether they would revive the celebrity version. In November 2023, ITV announced the relaunch of _Celebrity Big Brother_, beginning with the twenty-third series airing in March 2024 on ITV (ITV1 and STV). The show was rested in 2026, but was reportedly set to return in 2027. However, in July 2026, there have been unconfirmed reports that ITV had made the decision not to bring the show back for another series due to challenges ITV have been facing signing up big names to take part in the show.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-14)

#### Channel 4 (2001–2010)
who had risen to fame after appearing on _Big Brother 3_, enter the house as a housemate.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-33) The fifth series became the most controversial series to date, when accusations of racism towards housemate Shilpa Shetty arose against Goody and other housemates.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-35) Shetty ultimately went on to win the series, while Goody was evicted after spending two weeks in the house.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-37) Following the controversy surrounding the fifth series, _Celebrity Big Brother_ did not air in 2008.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-38) It did, however, return in 2009 and 2010, with the 2010 series being announced as the final one.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-39)

#### Channel 5 (2011–2018)
[edit]
After Richard Desmond bought Channel 5 in 2010, he said he was keen to acquire both _Big Brother_ and _Celebrity Big Brother_.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-40) Meanwhile, Endemol had been granted permission to keep the _Big Brother_ House at the Elstree TV Studios until 30 September 2013.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-Endemol_to_keep_BB_house_until_2013-41) On 2 April 2011, _The Daily Star_, a newspaper owned by Desmond's Northern & Shell company, reported that _Big Brother_ would be returning on Channel 5 in August 2011 with a Celebrity edition, followed by a main edition in September.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-dailystar.co.uk-42) Four days later, Channel 5 formally confirmed that it had signed a £200 million two-year contract with Endemol to screen _Big Brother_ from 18 August 2011.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-channel5.com-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-express.co.uk-44)_Big Brother 2_ winner Brian Dowling was announced as the new host.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-metro22jul2011-47) McCall declined the offer to host,

having said goodbye to the show in 2010.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-guardian.co.uk-48)_Celebrity Big Brother 8_ officially launched on 18 August 2011, and was won by Paddy Doherty.

In October 2023, the twentieth civilian series launched on ITV2 presented by AJ Odudu and Will Best, and several reports of a revival of _Celebrity Big Brother_ began to circulate.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-58) In November 2023, during a live eviction episode of the civilian series, it was announced that _Celebrity Big Brother_ would return on ITV in March 2024, presented by Odudu and Best. Unlike the civilian series, which is broadcast on ITV2, the celebrity series will air exclusively on ITV1 and STV.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-59) The show's spin off series _Celebrity Big Brother: Late & Live_ will air on ITV2, with the _Celebrity Big Brother: Live Stream_ airing daily on ITVX.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-60)

texts.1: _**Celebrity Big Brother**_ is a British television reality television based on the Dutch show _Big Brother_, created by producer [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") in 1997,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-BB1Article-1) which aired from 9 March 2001 to 10 September 2018, and again since 4 March 2024. The show follows a number of celebrity contestants, known as housemates, who were isolated from the outside world for an extended period of time in a custom-built house. Each week, one of the housemates is evicted by a public vote, with the last housemate named the winner. The series takes its name from the character in George Orwell's 1949 novel _Nineteen Eighty-Four_.
texts.2: _Celebrity Big Brother_ began as a one-time spin-off series to the original _Big Brother UK_ and premiered on Channel 4 on 9 March 2001. Following the successful first series, the show returned the following year for a second series. Though the show did not air for the next two years, it returned in 2005 and 2006. Following the highly controversial fifth series in 2007, the show did not return in 2008. It did air in 2009, but it was officially axed after the seventh series in 2010 when Channel 4 chose to cancel the programme as well as the main series.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-3) Despite this, it was picked up by Channel 5, and _Celebrity Big Brother_ returned in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-4) Between 2012 and 2018, two editions of _Celebrity Big Brother_ aired each year, with one airing in January and one airing following the conclusion of the civilian series in August. The show was initially hosted by Davina McCall from its inception to its cancellation by Channel 4. Despite being offered the position of host following the show's move to Channel 5, McCall chose not to return. Brian Dowling, who had won on _Big Brother 2_ and _Ultimate Big Brother_, replaced McCall as the host of the series.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-5) Dowling hosted the eighth to eleventh series, before being replaced by Emma Willis from the twelfth series until the show's cancellation on Channel 5 following the twenty-second series.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-6) Following the show's relaunch on ITV in March 2024, AJ Odudu and Will Best will host the show from the twenty-third series onwards.
texts.3:
Marcus Bentley has narrated the series since its inception in 2001.
Much like its predecessor, _Celebrity Big Brother_ was met with commercial success and has also received extensive media coverage and publicity since it premiered. It has been covered in spin-off series such as _Big Brother's Big Mouth_ and _Big Brother's Bit on the Side_, which also covered the main series.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-8) Similar to the parent series, _Celebrity Big Brother_ has been the source of much controversy and criticism, most notably during the 2007 series. Following this, a spin-off series known as _Big Brother: Celebrity Hijack_ aired in 2008 in the place of _Celebrity Big Brother_. _**Celebrity Big Brother**_ is a British television reality television based on the Dutch show _Big Brother_, created by producer [John de Mol Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_de_Mol_Jr. "John de Mol Jr.") in 1997,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-BB1Article-1) which aired from 9 March 2001 to 10 September 2018, and again since 4 March 2024. The show follows a number of celebrity contestants, known as housemates, who were isolated from the outside world for an extended period of time in a custom-built house. Each week, one of the housemates is evicted by a public vote, with the last housemate named the winner. The series takes its name from the character in George Orwell's 1949 novel _Nineteen Eighty-Four_.

_Celebrity Big Brother_ began as a one-time spin-off series to the original _Big Brother UK_ and premiered on Channel 4 on 9 March 2001. Following the successful first series, the show returned the following year for a second series. Though the show did not air for the next two years, it returned in 2005 and 2006. Following the highly controversial fifth series in 2007, the show did not return in 2008. It did air in 2009, but it was officially axed after the seventh series in 2010 when Channel 4 chose to cancel the programme as well as the main series.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-3) Despite this, it was picked up by Channel 5, and _Celebrity Big Brother_ returned in 2011.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity_Big_Brother_(British_TV_series)#cite_note-4) Between 2012 and 2018, two editions of _Celebrity Big Brother_ aired each year, with one airing in January and one airing following the conclusion of the civilian series in August.
